'''Flow Control''' is a ship [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effect]] that reduces the receiving module's power draw by '''10%'''. It can create a small amount of headroom in a tight power budget without changing the module's mass.<ref name="inara-effects">[https://inara.cz/elite/experimentaleffects/ INARA: Experimental effects], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref>

== Effect ==

Flow Control applies:

* '''Power draw:''' -10%

The reduction affects power supplied by the [[Power Plant]]. On a weapon, it does not reduce WEP-capacitor distributor draw, heat per shot, reload time, or ammunition use.

Because the percentage applies only to the modified module, the actual power saved depends on that module's existing draw. Fitting Flow Control to a high-draw module saves more power than applying it to a module that uses very little.

== Compatible modules ==

Flow Control is available for:

* [[Power Distributor|Power Distributors]];
* [[Shield Booster|Shield Boosters]];
* [[Shield Cell Bank|Shield Cell Banks]];
* conventional Engineer-compatible weapons, including lasers, multi-cannons, cannons, fragment cannons, plasma accelerators, rail guns, missiles, torpedoes, and mines.

Experimental weapons and mining tools do not normally accept the effect.<ref name="fandom-flow">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Flow_Control Elite Dangerous Wiki: Flow Control], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref>

Flow Control can be installed by an [[Engineers|Engineer]] whose workshop supports Engineering for the receiving module type. Experimental Effects must be applied at an Engineer workshop and cannot be pinned for [[Remote Engineering]].

== Materials ==

The material recipe depends on the receiving module family:

{| class="wikitable"
! Module family
! Required materials
|-
| Power Distributor
| 5 Phosphorus; 3 Heat Resistant Ceramics; 1 Conductive Polymers
|-
| Shield Booster
| 5 Inconsistent Shield Soak Analysis; 3 Security Firmware Patch; 3 Focus Crystals; 3 Niobium
|-
| Shield Cell Bank
| 5 Chemical Storage Units; 3 Chromium; 1 Conductive Polymers
|-
| Weapon
| 5 Mechanical Scrap; 3 Hybrid Capacitors; 1 Modified Embedded Firmware
|}

The materials are consumed once when the effect is applied. Replacing Flow Control with another Experimental Effect consumes the new effect's materials.

== When to use it ==

Flow Control is useful when a build is only slightly above its available power or when a Commander wants to preserve a lower-emission or better-protected Power Plant instead of moving to a higher-output configuration. Several individually small savings can add up when the effect is placed on multiple high-draw modules.

It is not a substitute for a deliberate power-priority plan. Modules assigned to lower priorities will still shut down when deployed power demand exceeds output, and a 10% reduction on a low-draw module may be too small to change that result.

Flow Control competes with direct performance effects. Weapons may gain more from damage, ammunition, or thermal effects; defensive modules may favour shield or integrity effects; and lightweight builds may prefer [[Stripped Down]]. Use Flow Control where its measured power saving enables the intended loadout.
